go to https://db.sp-tarkov.com, find all needed IDs, do a list. Then u go to “Advanced features” of SVM, add to “default IIC” next records per each 40mm ammo type: “id:StackMaxSize:xxx” where ID is a actual item ID from db and xxx is a desired number. 5485a8684bdc2da71d8b4567:StackMaxSize:xxx 5485a8684bdc2da71d8b4567:StackMaxRandom:xxx

and ALL ammo in game will have XXX stack size and all ammo drops in loot will have possible max stack size of XXX. Just do notice that ammo still have weight and u will need to split stacks ingame to really have ability to carry it or just decrease all ammo weight to 0 by adding into same block next record:

5485a8684bdc2da71d8b4567:Weight:0

PLEASE DISABLE AMMO STACK EDITING IN “INVENTORY AND ITEMS” TAB IF YOU GOING TO EDIT WITH PARENT SECTION

also wanna warn u not to edit limits to lower number that u’ve set earlier as it may lead to profile corrupt. (shall not, but still may) If u have question how it works - read FAQ section in SVM app

comments.body_html:
I managed to get it working, I was really just being dumb about it. I’m using this newer, universal (in the scope of linux desktops) packaging format known as flatpak for the Bottles app, and I hadn’t given it filesystem access.

My process for anyone who plays SPT on a Linux desktop and uses flatpaks (fedora, cachyOS, bazzite, SteamOS, can be installed on ubuntu as well as anything else):

  1. Grab SVM and unpack to your game directory (SPT-Linux tends to put this in ~/.local/share/Games/SPTarkov/ if you use a natively packaged version of steam (.rpm, .deb), and to ~/Games/tarkov/drive_c/SPTarkov/ if you use the unofficial Steam Flatpak from Flathub)
  2. Install Bottles (WINE Config manager GUI) and Flatseal (Flatpak configuration manager) from Flathub
  3. Launch Flatseal > navigate to Bottles in the apps list > head to the ‘Filesystem’ header > enable access to ‘All user files’ (filesystem=home)
  4. Close Flatseal and launch Bottles
  5. Select ‘Create New Bottle’ > name this however you’d prefer (I call it SVM) > change the WINE runner from soda-X.Y.Z to sys-wine-X.Y
  6. Once the bottle is created, select it > navigate to the ‘Options’ header > select ‘Dependencies’ > install dotnetcoredesktop9 (you can start typing to automatically filter the list)
  7. Head back and select ‘Run executable’ > select ‘Greed.exe’ to verify that your bottle config works (we’ll create an app shortcut next)
  8. Back within the Bottle settings, navigate to the ‘Programs’ header > select ‘Add Shortcuts…’ > select ‘Greed.exe’
  9. Select the three dot menu icon for Greed > select ‘Add Desktop Entry’, and now you should have an easy way to open the SVM configuration GUI.

Caveats & considerations:

  • This was based off my experience with Fedora 43 Workstation
  • If you’re using Ubuntu, you may need to install and enable Flatpak and the Flathub remote
  • Flatpak was preferred for Bottles due to self-contained dependencies, bearing in mind that repo WINE versions can vary
  • The soda-9.0.1 WINE runner selected by default in Bottles (at the time of writing) failed to launch the SVM GUI, even with the dotnet core 9 dependency in place.

comments.author: GhostFenixx
comments.body_html:
Limits of precision by floating point is to either include default value into it(like in case of some fields in Trader Services > Repair section) or just to give more freedom (Hideout section > multipliers were expanded by one digit by people requests), but apart from some rare cases it’s mostly either integers or doubles with 2 digits behind a point.

You are free to suggest which field limit can be expanded.

And yeah, i think i can add a global multiplier(including mod ones) of trader restock time, used to have per-trader, but removed due to lack of use and taking too much space.
